agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

_melody() {
    local i cur prev opts cmd
    COMPREPLY=()
    cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    prev="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD-1]}"
    cmd=""
    opts=""

    for i in ${COMP_WORDS[@]}
    do
        case "${cmd},${i}" in
            ",$1")
                cmd="melody"
                ;;
            *)
                ;;
        esac
    done

    case "${cmd}" in
        melody)
            opts="-o -n -r -t -f -h -V --output --no-color --repl --generate-completions --test --test-file --help --version [INPUT_FILE_PATH]"
            if [[ ${cur} == -* || ${COMP_CWORD} -eq 1 ]] ; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
                return 0
            fi
            case "${prev}" in
                --output)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                -o)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                --generate-completions)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                --test)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                -t)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                --test-file)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
---
#compdef melody

autoload -U is-at-least

_melody() {
    typeset -A opt_args
    typeset -a _arguments_options
    local ret=1

    if is-at-least 5.2; then
        _arguments_options=(-s -S -C)
    else
        _arguments_options=(-s -C)
    fi

    local context curcontext="$curcontext" state line
    _arguments "${_arguments_options[@]}" : \
'-o+[Write to a file]:OUTPUT_FILE_PATH:_default' \
'--output=[Write to a file]:OUTPUT_FILE_PATH:_default' \
'(-o --output -r --repl)--generate-completions=[Outputs completions for the selected shell To use, write the output to the appropriate location for your shell]:completions:_default' \
'(--generate-completions -r --repl -o --output)-t+[Test the compiled regex against a string]:test:_default' \
'(--generate-completions -r --repl -o --output)--test=[Test the compiled regex against a string]:test:_default' \
'(--generate-completions -r --repl -o --output -t --test)-f+[Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file]:test-file:_default' \
'(--generate-completions -r --repl -o --output -t --test)--test-file=[Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file]:test-file:_default' \
'-n[Print output with no color]' \
'--no-color[Print output with no color]' \
'-r[Start the Melody REPL]' \
'--repl[Start the Melody REPL]' \
'-h[Print help]' \
'--help[Print help]' \
'-V[Print version]' \
'--version[Print version]' \
'::input -- Read from a file
Use '\''-'\'' and or pipe input to read from stdin:_default' \
&& ret=0
}

(( $+functions[_melody_commands] )) ||
_melody_commands() {
    local commands; commands=()
    _describe -t commands 'melody commands' commands "$@"
}

if [ "$funcstack[1]" = "_melody" ]; then
    _melody "$@"
else
    compdef _melody melody
fi
</output>

---

using namespace System.Management.Automation
using namespace System.Management.Automation.Language

Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName 'melody' -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)

    $commandElements = $commandAst.CommandElements
    $command = @(
        'melody'
        for ($i = 1; $i -lt $commandElements.Count; $i++) {
            $element = $commandElements[$i]
            if ($element -isnot [StringConstantExpressionAst] -or
                $element.StringConstantType -ne [StringConstantType]::BareWord -or
                $element.Value.StartsWith('-') -or
                $element.Value -eq $wordToComplete) {
                break
        }
        $element.Value
    }) -join ';'

    $completions = @(switch ($command) {
        'melody' {
            [CompletionResult]::new('-o', '-o', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Write to a file')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--output', '--output', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Write to a file')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--generate-completions', '--generate-completions', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Outputs completions for the selected shell To use, write the output to the appropriate location for your shell')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-t', '-t', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against a string')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--test', '--test', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against a string')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-f', '-f', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--test-file', '--test-file', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file')
---

use builtin;
use str;

set edit:completion:arg-completer[melody] = {|@words|
    fn spaces {|n|
        builtin:repeat $n ' ' | str:join ''
    }
    fn cand {|text desc|
        edit:complex-candidate $text &display=$text' '(spaces (- 14 (wcswidth $text)))$desc
    }
    var command = 'melody'
    for word $words[1..-1] {
        if (str:has-prefix $word '-') {
            break
        }
        set command = $command';'$word
    }
    var completions = [
        &'melody'= {
            cand -o 'Write to a file'
            cand --output 'Write to a file'
            cand --generate-completions 'Outputs completions for the selected shell To use, write the output to the appropriate location for your shell'
            cand -t 'Test the compiled regex against a string'
            cand --test 'Test the compiled regex against a string'
            cand -f 'Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file'
            cand --test-file 'Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file'
            cand -n 'Print output with no color'
            cand --no-color 'Print output with no color'
            cand -r 'Start the Melody REPL'
</output>

}

    Match,
    Either,
    Capture(Option<String>),
}

    Ahead,
    Behind,
    NotAhead,
    NotBehind,

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Node {
    Literal(String),
    Raw(String),
    Symbol(Symbol),
    Category(String, bool), // (code, negated)
    Range(char, char, bool), // (from, to, negated)
    Quantifier(Quantifier, Box<Node>),
    Group(GroupKind, Vec<Node>),
    Assertion(AssertionKind, Vec<Node>),
    VarInvocation(String),
    VarDecl(String, Vec<Node>),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Quantifier {
    Exact(u64),
    Range(u64, u64),
    Over(u64),
    Some,
    Any,
    Option,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum GroupKind {
    Match,
    Either,
    Capture(Option<String>),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum AssertionKind {
    Ahead,
    Behind,
    NotAhead,
    NotBehind,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Symbol {
    Char,         // .
    Space,        // ' '
    Whitespace,   // \s or \S
    Digit,        // \d or \D
    Word,         // \w or \W
    Newline,      // \n
    Tab,          // \t
    Backspace,    // [\b]
    Return,       // \r
    Feed,         // \f
    Null,         // \0
    Vertical,     // \v
    Alphabetic,   // [a-zA-Z]
    Alphanumeric, // [a-zA-Z0-9]
    Boundary,     // \b or \B
    Start,        // ^
    End,          // $
}

impl Symbol {
    pub fn from_name(name: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match name {
            "char" => Some(Symbol::Char),
            "space" => Some(Symbol::Space),
            "whitespace" => Some(Symbol::Whitespace),
            "digit" => Some(Symbol::Digit),
            "word" => Some(Symbol::Word),
            "newline" => Some(Symbol::Newline),
            "tab" => Some(Symbol::Tab),
            "backspace" => Some(Symbol::Backspace),
            "return" => Some(Symbol::Return),
            "feed" => Some(Symbol::Feed),
            "null" => Some(Symbol::Null),
            "vertical" => Some(Symbol::Vertical),
            "alphabetic" => Some(Symbol::Alphabetic),
            "alphanumeric" => Some(Symbol::Alphanumeric),
            "boundary" => Some(Symbol::Boundary),
            "start" => Some(Symbol::Start),
            "end" => Some(Symbol::End),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}
EOF
